DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 137 s. 2022 October 20, 2022 HON. ABALOS MERRERA Ill Mayor, Binmaley Pangasinan Dear Mayor Merrera Ill: This pertains to your letter dated 25 July 2022 requesting for the Department's opinion on whether the purchase of a medical bus amounting to Php 1 1.7 M is subsumed under the term "medical ambulance" so that an Authority to Purchase (ATP) from this Department is no longer required. Baséd on the documents forwarded to this Department, the antecedent facts are as follows: • The Municipality of Binmaley, Pangasinan, allegedly purchased one (I) unit of brand-new medical bus which amounted to Eleven Million Seven Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 11.7M) • The said medical bus had been subject to a request dated 13 July 2022 for comprehensive audit and inspection by the Commission on Audit (COA) through the regional office in La Union, Pangasinan. • Reportedly, in the course of an internal audit during the transition period, it was found that said purchase lacked Authority to Purchase (ATP) from the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG). The Municipal Local Government Operations Officer (MLGOO) was said to have been consulted which in turn presented a Circular from the Department of Budget and Management stating that purchases of medical ambulance by the Local Government Unit will no longer require ATP from the DILG and the approving authority for the purchase is now the Local Chief Executive. Foremost, to be able to assess and answer the query on whether the purchased medical bus amounting to Php 11.7M is subsumed under the term "medical ambulance", requires comprehensive audit of the vehicle, both the pertinent documents thereof and the actual physical medical equipment therein and its functions. Thus, aside from the fact that the documents forwarded to this Department do not provide with sufficient bases for this level to provide a sound response on the matter, the same falls within the expertise and authority of the Commission on Audit (COA) and the evaluation of the evaluation of the Department of Health (if necessary subject to COA's discretion), not with this Department. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Under DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-01, dated 4 March 2010, as supplemented by Memorandum Order No. 2010-02, dated 17 September 2010, the following are matters ought not to be addressed by this Department, viz: (1) those containing facts that are justiciable in nature; (2) those presumptively valid acts e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; (3) those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation; and (4) those that are cognizable by other agencies Of the government. It may be prudent to take cognizance of the submission that the assailed medical bus has already been subjected to a request for audit and inspection by the Commission on Audit (COA). In view thereof, we respectfully recommend for the concerned LGU to wait for COA's Audit Investigation Report on the matter. Now, without delving on the technicality of the classification of whether the åssailed medical bus is an ordinary vehicle or considered a medical ambulance, may we provide you with the applicable policy insofar as the Department is concerned, the DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2021-004 dated 18 January 2021. The salient provision of thereof is as follows: 5.1.3 All LGUs with proposed acquisition of motor vehicles that are not under the approving authority of the Local Chief Executive must seek prior approval from the Secretary of Budget and Management, the Office of the President, or the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government, on specific motor vehicles as may be authorized pursuant to Item 5.3 hereof. The •approving authority is given to the Local Chief Executives only in cases of unencumbered local funds as funding source pursuant to Item 5.3.2. which is subject to specified limitations set forth in Presidential Administrative Order No. 14 and DBM Budget Circular No. 2017-1, to wit: 5.3.2 Unencumbered local funds: 5.3.2.1 Local Chief Executives (i.e. Provincial Governors, City Mayors, Municipal Mayors, and Punong Barangays) for the acquisition of the specification of the following motor vehicles and heavy equipment, based on the specification limitations set forth in Presidential Administrative Order No. 14 and DBM Budget Circular No. 2017-1 (dated December 10, 2018 and April 26, 2017, respectively. Specific-purpose vehicles, such as, medical ambulances, 5.3.2.1.1 military and police patrol vehicles, armored vehicles, prisoner's vans, and fire trucks; 5.3.2.1.2 Heavy equipment such as, road construction equipment, cargo transport equipment, farm machineries, waste management or and similar environmental sanitation equipment, other vehicles/equipment; Page 2 of 3

5.3.2.1.3 5.3.2.1.4 5.3.2.1.5 Locally-assembled owner- or passenger-type jeep; Motorized banca and/or motorized boats; Vehicles for mass transport when necessary in the interest of public service; and 5.3.2.1.6 Motorcycles and tri-wheel vehicles We submit that a Medical Bus is not within the aforementioned enumeration. However, considering the query herein on whether the same be considered as medical ambulance, the audit investigation result of the Commission on Audit and/or other competent authorities must be anticipated. In the event the COA and/or the competent court declares the assailed Medical Bus as not subsumed under the term "medical ambulance" or not falling within any other categories in the aforementioned enumeration of vehicles that may be purchased with the sole authority of the Local Chief Executive, it follows that the approval of the Secretary of Budget and Management and Secretary of the Interior and Local Government should have been secured pursuant to Item 5.3. I of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2021-004 dated 18 January 2021. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Ve A yours, ICTOR R.
